newsitem.title: USA: Sierra to sell modem chipset business.
newsitem.headline: Sierra to sell modem chipset business.

text.p: Sierra Semiconductor Corp said Wednesday it will exit the modem chipset business, sell its product line and take a $50 to $80 million charge against its earnings in the quarter ending September 30.
"The decision to no longer participate in modem chipset products is based on the status of the PC Modem business today," James Diller, chief executive said in a statement.

Diller said heightened competition is pressuring prices and margins, inventories in distribution channels are increasing and supply is building. He added the company sees no signs those trends will reverse.
Sierra Semiconductor, a maker of semiconductor chips, said it will now focus on manufacturing products for computer infrastructure and networking markets.

"The networking semiconductor market, in particular, has experienced significant growth during the last few years, and industry analysts have projected future growth in demand for networking chips and chipsets," Diller said.
Due to the change in business focus, president and chief operating officer Richard Koeltl will leave the company. Diller will assume his duties.
The company said the exact size of the charge will be determined throughout the quarter and will be announced in its thrid quarter earnings release, scheduled for October.
Sierra ended trading today off 1/4 at 9-1/4.
